title: Palantir, Nvidia and Nebius Push 'Sovereign AI' From Policy Slogan Into Enterprise Supply Chains
subhead: Palantir launched a 'Sovereign AI Supply Chain Platform' with Nvidia, named Nebius its preferred sovereign AI infrastructure partner, and expanded a Japan push with Fujitsu — an enterprise-scale bid to let companies own their AI stacks rather than rent them from hyperscalers.

sections.heading: Palantir and Nvidia Turn 'Sovereign AI' Into a Supply-Chain Product
sections.body: On Sept. 10, Palantir and Nvidia announced a 'Sovereign AI Supply Chain Platform', and immediately dogfooded it inside Nvidia's own operations. According to The Next Web and HPCwire, the platform starts with Nvidia's internal supply chain — a move 24/7 Wall St. framed as handing a roughly 1.3 million-part supply chain over to Palantir's software. The New Stack reported the two companies fine-tuned a 30-billion-parameter Nemotron model for Nvidia's supply chain, with Nvidia saying it outperformed a model about 18 times its size on the task. The announcement came at Palantir's customer forum, alongside expanded ties with Cisco and the U.S. FAA, per Investor's Business Daily.
sections.whyItMatters: This shifts 'sovereign AI' from vague policy talk among governments into a concrete, commercial enterprise offering — and Nvidia choosing itself as the first customer gives the product immediate credibility and a reference deployment.

sections.heading: Nebius Selected as Palantir's Preferred Sovereign AI Infrastructure Partner
sections.body: Days earlier, on Sept. 8, Palantir named Nebius — the Nvidia-backed, Amsterdam-headquartered AI cloud — its preferred sovereign AI infrastructure partner, according to Data Center Dynamics, Seeking Alpha and TipRanks. The companies said they would deliver a complete 'sovereign AI stack' to Palantir's commercial customers, letting enterprises train and run models on infrastructure they effectively own rather than rent from hyperscalers (a point marketbeat.com summarized as Palantir and Nebius 'cutting the cloud cord'). Yahoo Finance reported Nebius shares rose roughly 6-8% on the news, while Palantir shares slipped on concerns about valuation and margin, per 24/7 Wall St.
sections.whyItMatters: Nebius is positioning against the largest US cloud providers by selling enterprises ownership of their training compute — a bet that 'AI sovereignty' is now a selling point in the B2B market, not just a government procurement theme.

sections.heading: Palantir Deepens AI Push in Japan With Fujitsu
sections.body: Palantir also expanded its Japan partnership with Fujitsu on Sept. 10, with Fujitsu becoming a global 'FDE' (forward-deployed engineering) partner under a new AIP agreement, per Yahoo Finance, Unite.AI and Investing.com. The companies framed the renewal around advancing sovereign AI and enterprise digital transformation in Japan, a sign Palantir is leaning on regional partners to distribute its AI platform outside the US.
sections.whyItMatters: Japan is a key test market for data-sovereignty-driven AI adoption — Fujitsu gives Palantir a distribution channel into regulated Japanese enterprises that may be wary of sending data to US-hosted clouds.

sections.heading: Mistral Raises Record €3 Billion as Europe Chases Sovereign AI
sections.body: The sovereign AI push reached funding in Europe too. French AI lab Mistral closed what Proactive Financial News called a record €3 billion raise, described by AI Business as a bridge to sovereign AI and by PYMNTS as part of a Cloudera partnership to meet sovereign enterprise AI demand. Mistral also appears in the space story below, joining a $1 billion orbital AI project. The raise signals Europe's leading frontier-lab bet that building its own AI stack — and selling that capacity to regional enterprises and states — is viable against US incumbents.
sections.whyItMatters: Mistral's scale of funding and its pairing with infrastructure partners (Cloudera, Loft Orbital) shows European 'AI autonomy' is being built commercially and in space, not just through Brussels regulation.

sections.heading: Space: UAE, France and Mistral Back a $1 Billion 50-Satellite AI Constellation
sections.body: On Sept. 9, a consortium including Abu Dhabi's Marlan Space, US-French operator Loft Orbital and Mistral announced a projected $1 billion, 50-satellite AI-enabled imaging constellation, per SpaceNews (Jeff Foust) and Via Satellite. Data Center Dynamics reported it as a deal to 'put compute in space,' serving France, Europe and the UAE, with satellites built in Abu Dhabi. Fast Company Middle East said the aim is to cut space-data response times from hours to seconds; TradeArabia and Arabian Business cited the 'Altair-Next Gen' program. The Arab Weekly weighed the strategic meaning of AI in space for the Gulf.
sections.whyItMatters: This puts on-orbit AI compute — not just imaging — at the center of a Gulf-Europe space partnership, giving the UAE a tangible stake in the AI-space value chain and positioning Abu Dhabi alongside France in orbital AI infrastructure.

sections.heading: Launch: Stoke Space Raises $1 Billion to Take On SpaceX on Reusability
sections.body: Privately, launch economics stayed contested. Stoke Space raised a $1 billion Series E (Reuters, TechCrunch, GeekWire) to fund its fully reusable Nova rocket and a more powerful upsize, targeting a first launch as early as 2027 — a direct challenge to SpaceX on re-flying rockets. Space.com and SpaceWatch.GLOBAL noted the round's size and Stoke's Moses Lake, Washington testing program.
sections.whyItMatters: Launch capacity and reusability remain the bottleneck to the satellite constellations — both imaging and AI — that states and firms are racing to deploy, so Stoke's capital position matters for the broader orbital-power picture.

bottomLine: The defining development this week is 'sovereign AI' converting from a policy slogan into a commercial market. Palantir and Nvidia launched a sovereign AI supply-chain platform beginning with Nvidia's own operations; Palantir named Nvidia-backed Nebius its preferred sovereign AI infrastructure partner, expanding into Japan via Fujitsu; Mistral raised a record €3 billion; and a UAE-France-Mistral consortium committed $1 billion to a 50-satellite AI constellation. The through-line is enterprise and state buyers moving away from renting AI from hyperscalers toward owning their compute and data stacks — in data centers and, increasingly, in orbit.
